mainTopic: The שכינה among an impure Israel, a היקש learned from a היקש, sprinkling toward the פרוכת, and what to do when the bull's and goat's blood are mixed on יום הכפורים.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a story: a מין taunts רבי חנינא that the Jewish people are impure, so the שכינה has left them. רבי חנינא answers from a פסוק that the שכינה stays with them even in their impurity. The גמרא then returns to the יום הכפורים sprinklings and asks how a law learned by היקש can teach another היקש. It gives several answers: הימנו ודבר אחר, then that the second comparison is about places, then that everything is learned in one single comparison. Next, a ברייתא says the blood is sprinkled facing the פרוכת, not on it. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי reports blood drops he saw on the curtain in Rome, and the גמרא explains that the order of the drops showed which offerings they came from. Finally, the גמרא asks what to do if the bull's blood and the goat's blood got mixed. רבא's answer and רב פפא's suggestion are both rejected because they break the order the תורה requires: the bull before the goat, and upward before downward for each animal. רבי ירמיה's answer of two full sets of sprinklings keeps that order.

steps.title: The heretic claims the Jews are impure
steps.stepSummary: The מין tells רבי חנינא that the Jewish people are definitely impure now, citing a פסוק from איכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now you are certainly impure, as it is written: 'Her impurity is in her skirts.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a story. A heretic is taunting רבי חנינא by claiming that the Jewish people are impure, so the שכינה can no longer be among them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the story, the heretic implied that the שכינה cannot rest on an impure people. Here he 'proves' that the Jews are impure, using the פסוק in איכה about Jerusalem's impurity. His point is that the שכינה has left Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: certainly, definitely
ritually impure
'her impurity is in her skirts' (איכה א:ט)
as it is written

phrases.english: Now you are certainly impure,
phrases.notes: The heretic is speaking to רבי חנינא about the Jewish people.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'Her impurity is in her skirts.'
phrases.notes: איכה א:ט

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בָּרִי טְמֵאִים אַתּוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the heretic and רבי חנינא from the previous section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the שכינה is still present among the Jewish people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Jews are impure according to a פסוק, and the שכינה does not rest on impurity, so the שכינה must have left them.

steps.title: The Divine Presence stays even amid impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers from a פסוק in ויקרא that the שכינה dwells among Israel even when they are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Come and see what is written about them: 'That dwells with them in the midst of their impurity.' Even when they are impure, the שכינה rests among them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the heretic. He uses a פסוק that says ה׳ dwells with Israel even in the middle of their impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא does not deny that Israel can be impure. Instead, he denies that impurity drives the שכינה away. The פסוק 'השוכן אתם בתוך טומאתם' openly says that the שכינה stays with them even then.

keyTerms.meaning: come and see
'Who dwells with them in the midst of their impurity' (ויקרא טז:טז)
the Divine Presence
rests, dwells

steps.whatToRemember: The heretic's argument is that impurity means the שכינה has left. רבי חנינא's answer is that the שכינה stays with Israel even in their impurity.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof verse comes from the very פרשה of the עבודת יום הכיפורים that this סוגיא is studying. That is why the story was brought here.

phrases.english: He said to him: Come and see
phrases.notes: רבי חנינא answers the heretic.

phrases.english: what is written about them:
'That dwells with them in the midst of their impurity,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:טז

phrases.english: even at a time when they are impure —
the Divine Presence dwells among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, תָּא חֲזִי מָה כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the heretic's claim in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-verse showing that the assumption behind the claim is wrong.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Impurity drives the שכינה away from Israel.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שכינה remains among Israel even when they are impure.

steps.title: Can a law learned by comparison teach another comparison?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the sprinkling laws. It asks how a law learned through a היקש can then be used to teach another law through a היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can something that is learned through a היקש turn around and teach through a היקש?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא goes back to the halachic discussion about the blood sprinklings. It raises a problem with how the earlier laws were learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the sprinkling pattern (one upward, seven downward) for the פר and the שעיר was learned by comparing them to each other (a היקש). Then the sprinklings toward the פרוכת were learned from that result by another comparison. In קדשים there is a rule that a law learned by היקש cannot itself teach by היקש, so this second step seems invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: a comparison of two topics that the תורה places side by side, so that laws pass from one to the other
a law that is derived (not written explicitly)
turns around and teaches
but can it be that (introduces a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: This rule (a learned law cannot teach again by היקש) is a special rule for קדשים, the laws of offerings. Do not assume it applies the same way in every area of halacha.

phrases.english: But does a matter that is learned through a juxtaposition,
turn around and teach through a juxtaposition?
phrases.notes: In קדשים this is normally not allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story behind and returns to the halachic discussion of the sprinklings from before the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier derivation of the sprinklings toward the פרוכת through a second comparison.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In קדשים, a law derived by היקש may not serve as the source for another היקש. Here a second comparison is built on the result of the first.

steps.title: The first comparison was not a full comparison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the law was learned partly from its own פסוק and partly from the comparison (הימנו ודבר אחר), so it does not count as a real היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This law comes from itself and from something else, so it is not considered a היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The first derivation was not purely a היקש, because much of the law is already written in its own place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic idea of sprinkling upward and downward is written explicitly for both the פר and the שעיר. The comparison was only needed to fill in a detail, the exact number of sprinklings. Since the law comes 'from itself and from something else,' it is not treated as a learned-by-היקש law, so it can still teach further.

keyTerms.meaning: from itself and from something else, meaning a law partly written in its own place and partly learned from elsewhere
is not considered

phrases.english: This is a case of 'from itself and something else,'
phrases.notes: The sprinkling is written for each offering. Only the number was learned from the other.

phrases.english: and it is not considered a juxtaposition.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי, הֵימֶנּוּ וְדָבָר אַחֵר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the first derivation so that it falls outside the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sprinkling law was learned entirely through a היקש, so it cannot teach again.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the law comes partly from its own פסוק (הימנו ודבר אחר), it is not a full היקש and may teach further.

steps.title: The answer only works for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the last answer works only for the opinion that הימנו ודבר אחר is not a היקש. It asks what to say according to the opinion that it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says it is not a היקש. But according to the one who says it is a היקש, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. It points out that there is a disagreement on this point, and the answer fails for one side. This sets up the next answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute about whether a law that comes 'from itself and from something else' counts as a היקש. For the opinion that it does count, the challenge of step 3 comes back in full force. The גמרא now needs a different solution for that opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: this works well (for one view)
according to the one who says
what can be said?

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says
it is not considered a juxtaposition.
But according to the one who says it is considered a juxtaposition,
what can be said?
phrases.notes: The answer comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא הָוֵי הֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 4 to one opinion and reopens the challenge of step 3 for the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4 (הימנו ודבר אחר).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the opinion that הימנו ודבר אחר is a real היקש, the first derivation is still a היקש. So the original problem of step 3 returns.

steps.title: The two comparisons are about different things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one comparison links the animals and the other links the places, so no law learned by היקש is teaching another היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the locations that are learned from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5. Even if הימנו ודבר אחר counts as a real היקש, there is no problem here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate comparisons. One compares the bull's blood to the goat's blood. The other compares sprinkling outside the curtain to sprinkling inside. They do not build on each other, so this is not a היקש learned from another היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: Places or locations: here, inside the קודש הקדשים and outside it, near the curtain
They are learned from each other
A comparison between two things placed together in the תורה, so that laws pass from one to the other

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is cancelling the rule that a law learned by היקש cannot teach another היקש. The rule stays in place. The גמרא is showing that this case never breaks it.

phrases.english: It is the locations
phrases.notes: Inside and outside the curtain

phrases.english: that are learned from one another.
phrases.notes: Not the animals: that is a separate comparison

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקוֹמוֹת הוּא דְּגָמְרִי מֵהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5 according to the opinion that הימנו ודבר אחר is a היקש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what is being compared: the two היקשים have different subjects.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the second comparison was built on the first, making a chain of היקש from היקש.
steps.terutzMaskana: One היקש compares the animals and the other compares the places. They are independent, so there is no chain.

steps.title: Inside and outside learned in one single comparison
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the outside sprinkling was learned from the inside sprinkling all at once, as part of one combined היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: outside is learned from inside in one single time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to answer the same question from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there are not two separate steps at all. One single comparison covers the bull, the goat, and both places together. Since nothing is learned in two stages, the problem of a היקש learned from a היקש never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another possible answer
Outside: the sprinkling in the היכל, facing the curtain
Inside: the sprinkling in the קודש הקדשים
All at once, in one single learning

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the same problem: (1) the two comparisons are about different things (animals versus places); (2) it is one combined comparison made all at once. Either way, no היקש is learned from another היקש.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
phrases.notes: Introduces an alternative answer

phrases.english: outside from inside
phrases.notes: The sprinkling outside is learned from the sprinkling inside

phrases.english: he learns all at one time.
phrases.notes: One combined comparison, not two stages

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 5's question, alongside Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Merging into one comparison: a single היקש rather than two linked ones.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought there were two stages of learning, one built on the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything is learned at once in a single היקש, so there is no chain.

steps.title: Sprinkling facing the curtain, not on it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the כהן גדול sprinkles the blood facing the curtain, without touching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sage taught: when he sprinkles, he does not sprinkle on the curtain, but facing the curtain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by bringing a ברייתא about where the blood lands when it is sprinkled outside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the blood is aimed toward the curtain, but it does not have to land on the curtain itself. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage taught: introduces a ברייתא
Sprinkles the blood
The curtain separating the היכל from the קודש הקדשים
Facing, opposite

phrases.english: A sage taught: when he sprinkles,
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול sprinkling the blood outside the curtain

phrases.english: he does not sprinkle on the curtain,
but facing the curtain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא מַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new point about the sprinkling: where exactly the blood lands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood is sprinkled toward the curtain, not on it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר saw blood on the curtain in Rome
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי testifies that he saw the curtain in Rome, with blood drops on it from the יום הכפורים bull and goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי said: I saw it in Rome, and there were several drops of blood on it from the bull and goat of יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A sage challenges the ברייתא with something he saw with his own eyes. The blood seems to have actually landed on the curtain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood only had to be sprinkled facing the curtain, why were there drops on the curtain itself? His eyewitness report suggests the sprinkling did reach the curtain.

keyTerms.meaning: Rome, where the Romans brought the Temple vessels
Drops of blood
The bull and goat of יום הכפורים

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei said:
I saw it in Rome,
phrases.notes: The curtain, taken by the Romans

phrases.english: and on it were several drops of blood

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל פַּר וְשָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: of the bull and goat of Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֲנִי רְאִיתִיהָ בְּרוֹמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of Step 8 with eyewitness evidence.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that the blood is sprinkled facing the curtain, not on it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Physical evidence: blood from the יום הכפורים offerings was found on the curtain, so the blood must have been sprinkled on it.

steps.title: Maybe the blood came from other offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the drops may have come from the bull of פר העלם דבר של צבור or the goats of עבודה זרה, not from יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they were from the bull for a mistaken communal sin and the goats for idol worship!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רבי אלעזר's evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of other offerings is also sprinkled toward the curtain. So the drops he saw prove nothing about יום הכפורים. Perhaps those other offerings went onto the curtain while the יום הכפורים blood did not.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps: introduces another possibility that weakens a proof
The bull brought when the community sinned by mistake, following a wrong ruling of the בית דין
The goats brought for a communal mistaken sin of idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי אלעזר made up what he saw. It only questions which offerings the blood came from.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִילְמָא דְּפַר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר
phrases.english: But perhaps they were of the bull for an unwitting communal sin
phrases.notes: Its blood is also sprinkled toward the curtain

phrases.english: and the goats for idol worship!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא דְּפַר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the evidence in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the blood drops seen in Rome.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The drops cannot be identified as יום הכפורים blood, since other offerings are also sprinkled toward the curtain.

steps.title: The drops were lined up in order, so they came from יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's proof. He saw that the drops were arranged in their proper order, and only the יום הכפורים service is done that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw that they were made in their order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the rejection from step 10. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי knew the drops were from יום הכפורים because they were neatly lined up in sequence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 suggested the drops might have come from פר העלם דבר של צבור or the goats of עבודה זרה. The answer is that on יום הכפורים the sprinklings are counted in a fixed order, one after another, which leaves an orderly row of drops. The other offerings have no such order, so an orderly row points to יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: in their order, in proper sequence
that he saw
they were made or done

phrases.english: For he saw that they were made in their order.
phrases.notes: In their order means one drop after another, the way the sprinklings are counted on יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּחֲזָא דַּעֲבִידִי כְּסִדְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the answer in step 10 and restores the challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual detail identifies the source of the drops
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The drops could have come from other offerings that are sprinkled toward the curtain.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drops were in an orderly sequence, and only יום הכפורים has that sequence, so they came from יום הכפורים.

steps.title: A matching teaching about the communal error bull
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a parallel teaching about פר העלם דבר של צבור. When the כהן sprinkles it, the blood is not supposed to touch the curtain, but if it does touch, nothing is ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned something similar about the bull brought for a communal error: when he sprinkles, they would not touch the curtain, and if they touched, they touched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cites a second source with the same rule, this time about פר העלם דבר של צבור. It is also setting up the parallel story about drops on the curtain from that offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as on יום הכפורים, the blood of פר העלם דבר is sprinkled facing the curtain and is not meant to touch it. The phrase 'if they touched, they touched' means that touching does not make the service invalid. This explains how drops could still end up on the curtain.

keyTerms.meaning: the bull brought when the community sinned by mistake because of a wrong court ruling
the curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים
sprinkles
and we also learned in a משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that touching the curtain is not ideal but does not invalidate the service.

phrases.english: And we also learned regarding
the bull for a communal unwitting sin
something like this:
when he sprinkles,
they (the drops) would not touch the curtain,
but if they touched, they touched.
phrases.notes: Meaning: no harm is done, and the service is still valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel teaching about a different offering that matches the ברייתא in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For פר העלם דבר של צבור, the blood is not supposed to touch the curtain, but if it does, the service is still valid.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר saw drops from the communal offerings in Rome
steps.stepSummary: In this parallel teaching, רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי testifies that the curtain he saw in Rome had drops from פר העלם דבר של צבור and the goats of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי said: I saw it in Rome, and on it were several drops of blood from the communal error bull and from the idolatry goats.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the parallel teaching, the same eyewitness gives testimony, but here he says the drops came from the communal offerings. The גמרא is setting up a question about how he knew that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא really does repeat the testimony from step 9 here, but this time it belongs to the teaching about פר העלם דבר. Now he names פר העלם דבר and שעירי עבודה זרה as the source of the drops, instead of יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rome, where the Temple vessels were taken
drops of blood
the goats brought when the community worshipped idols by mistake

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of step 9. It is the same witness quoted in a different teaching, and here he identifies different offerings as the source of the drops.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei said:
I saw it (the curtain) in Rome,
and there were on it several drops of blood

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: from the bull for a communal unwitting sin,
and from the goats for idolatry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֲנִי רְאִיתִיהָ בְּרוֹמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the parallel teaching with eyewitness testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drops from the communal offerings were seen on the curtain.

steps.title: Maybe those drops were really from יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the testimony: how did he know the drops were from the communal offerings and not from the bull and goat of יום הכפורים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they were from the bull and goat of יום הכפורים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how the witness identified the drops. Blood from יום הכפורים also lands near the curtain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 10. There, the question was whether יום הכפורים drops might be from the communal offerings. Here, the question is whether the communal drops might be from יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: but perhaps
they are

phrases.english: But perhaps they are from the bull and goat
of Yom Kippur?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא דְּפַר וְשָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification made in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the witness identified the drops as coming from the communal offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Several offerings put blood near the curtain, so the drops could have come from יום הכפורים instead.

steps.title: The drops were not in order, so they were not from יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: He saw that the drops were scattered and not in sequence. That fits the communal offerings, not יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For he saw that they were made not in their order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the drops were scattered and out of order. יום הכפורים drops would have been in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same test as step 11. Orderly drops point to יום הכפורים, and disorderly drops point to the communal offerings, which have no counting order.

keyTerms.meaning: not in their order

steps.whatToRemember: The order of the drops tells you where they came from: orderly drops mean יום הכפורים, and scattered drops mean פר העלם דבר or שעירי עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: For he saw that they were made not in their order.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּחֲזַנְהוּ דַּעֲבִידִי שֶׁלֹּא כְּסִדְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual detail identifies the source of the drops
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The drops might have come from יום הכפורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drops were out of order, so they came from the communal offerings.

steps.title: What if the bull's blood and the goat's blood got mixed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: what should the כהן גדול do if the bull's blood and the goat's blood got mixed together?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the bloods became mixed for him, blood with blood...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new practical case about the יום הכפורים sprinklings. This line sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן גדול sprinkles the bull's blood (one up, seven down) and then the goat's blood. If the two bloods were mixed before he finished, it is unclear how he can sprinkle each animal's blood properly.

keyTerms.meaning: became mixed
blood with blood (here, the bull's blood with the goat's blood)

phrases.english: If the bloods became mixed for him, blood with blood,

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְעָרְבוּ לוֹ דָּמִים בְּדָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the sprinkling procedure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the כהן גדול should sprinkle when the bull's blood and the goat's blood are mixed

steps.title: רבא: one set of sprinklings counts for both
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the כהן גדול sprinkles once upward and seven times downward from the mixture, and this counts for both the bull and the goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He gives one upward and seven downward, and it counts for him for this one and for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The mixture contains both bloods, so one set of sprinklings covers both animals at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every sprinkling from the mixture contains some blood of the bull and some blood of the goat. So rather than doing two separate sets, רבא says one set of one up and seven down fulfills the job for both animals.

keyTerms.meaning: upward (the one upper sprinkling)
downward (the seven lower sprinklings)
it counts for both this one and that one

phrases.english: Rava said:
He gives one upward and seven downward,
and it counts for him for this one and for that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: נוֹתֵן אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One set of sprinklings (one up, seven down) from the mixture counts for both the bull and the goat.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: this breaks the order the תורה requires
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה harshly rejects רבא's answer. With the mixture, the goat's upward sprinkling would happen before the bull's downward sprinklings, but the תורה requires finishing all of the bull's blood first.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said it before רבי ירמיה. He said: Foolish Babylonians! Because they live in a dark land, they say dark teachings. He is giving the goat's upward sprinkling before the bull's downward ones, and the תורה said 'And when he finishes atoning for the holy place': finish the bull's blood, and only then finish the goat's blood!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבא's answer. Mixing the sprinklings ruins the order the Torah requires between the bull and the goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the כהן גדול does the upward sprinkling from the mixture, he is already sprinkling the goat's upward blood. But at that moment the bull's seven downward sprinklings are not yet done. The verse 'וכלה מכפר את הקדש' teaches that the bull's blood must be completely finished before any of the goat's blood is sprinkled.

keyTerms.meaning: foolish Babylonians
a dark land (Babylonia, which is low-lying)
dark (unclear, illogical) teachings
and when he finishes atoning for the holy place (ויקרא ט״ז:כ׳)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not saying the mixture fails to contain both bloods. His problem is the order: the goat's sprinkling would start before the bull's sprinklings are finished.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the sequence of the יום הכפורים sprinklings is a requirement from the תורה, not just a matter of convenience.

phrases.english: They said it before Rabbi Yirmeya,
he said: Foolish Babylonians!
Because they live in a dark land,
they say dark teachings!
Look, he is giving the upward sprinkling of the goat
before the downward sprinklings of the bull,
and the Torah said:
'And when he finishes atoning for the holy place,'
meaning: finish the blood of the bull,
and afterward finish the blood of the goat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה, אָמַר: בַּבְלָאֵי טַפְשָׁאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that one set of sprinklings from the mixture counts for both animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The upward sprinkling from the mixture already includes the goat's blood before the bull's downward sprinklings are done. That breaks the order required by the verse וכלה מכפר את הקדש.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's solution: two full sets of sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rules that the כהן גדול does a full set (one up, seven down) for the פר, and then a full new set (one up, seven down) for the שעיר, all from the mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי ירמיה said: He gives one upward and seven downward for the sake of the bull, and then gives again one upward and seven downward for the sake of the goat.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבא's answer, רבי ירמיה now gives his own answer to the question of mixed blood: two complete, separate sets of sprinklings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the order the תורה requires: all of the פר's sprinklings are finished before any of the שעיר's begin. Even though every sprinkling contains both bloods, what counts is what the כהן גדול has in mind (לשם). During the first set the goat's blood in the mixture simply does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a replacement answer)
For the sake of, with the intention of
And he goes back and gives again
The bull offering of the כהן גדול
The goat offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the first set 'uses up' the goat's blood. The blood is mixed, but intention decides which offering a sprinkling counts for, so the goat's blood in the first set is treated as if it was never sprinkled.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in קדשים, intention (לשם) can define which offering a sprinkling belongs to, even when the bloods are physically mixed.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yirmeya said:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה לְשֵׁם הַפָּר,
phrases.english: He gives one upward and seven downward for the sake of the bull,
and he goes back and gives one upward
and seven downward for the sake of the goat.
phrases.notes: A second full set, so the goat's order (up, then down) is also kept.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected answer with a solution that avoids the order problem raised in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two complete sets of sprinklings from the mixture: one for the פר, then one for the שעיר.

steps.title: New case: the blood got mixed during the later sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new case: the bloods got mixed partway through, during the later sprinklings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the bloods became mixed for him during the later sprinklings, what does he do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new case. This time the mixing happened during the final sprinklings in the היכל, toward the curtain. As רב פפא's proposal in the next step shows, the פר's upward sprinkling there had already been given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now part of the פר's job is already finished. So the question is how to complete the rest without breaking the required order for either animal.

keyTerms.meaning: They became mixed
Blood with blood (the פר's blood with the שעיר's blood)
The final set of sprinklings, done in the היכל toward the פרוכת (as opposed to the earlier ones inside the קודש הקדשים)

phrases.english: If the bloods became mixed for him, blood with blood,
during the later sprinklings,
phrases.notes: This is the last set, done in the היכל toward the פרוכת. רב פפא's plan next assumes the bull's upward sprinkling there came before the mixing.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְעָרְבוּ לוֹ דָּמִים בְּדָמִים בְּמַתָּנוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mixing at the start (steps 16-19) to mixing in the middle of the sprinklings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to finish the sprinklings when the bloods mixed after the פר's upward sprinkling was already given.

steps.title: רב פפא's suggested shortcut
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא thinks the seven downward sprinklings can count for both the פר and the שעיר, followed by one upward sprinkling for the שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, sitting before רבא, thought to say: He gives seven downward for the sake of the bull and for the sake of the goat, and then gives one upward for the sake of the goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a quick answer to the new case: let one set of seven downward sprinklings count for both animals, then add the goat's upward one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His idea makes sense for the פר: its upward was already done, so its downward ones are next. But for the שעיר, this puts its downward sprinklings before its upward one. The next step attacks exactly that point.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought, he was inclined to
Before him, in his presence
To say

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa, before Rava, thought to say:
He gives seven downward
for the sake of the bull and for the sake of the goat,
and he then gives one upward
for the sake of the goat.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the new case raised in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seven downward sprinklings for both the פר and the שעיר, then one upward sprinkling for the שעיר.

steps.title: רבא sharply rejects רב פפא's shortcut
steps.stepSummary: רבא scolds רב פפא for repeating the same mistake רבי ירמיה already exposed: his plan puts the שעיר's downward sprinklings before its upward one, against the order the תורה requires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Until now they called us fools, and now they will call us fools of fools, because we teach them and they do not learn. Look, he is giving the goat's downward sprinklings before the goat's upward one, and the תורה said: give upward, and after that downward!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב פפא's suggestion with a strong rebuke, then points out the exact flaw: the goat's order is broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same principle רבי ירמיה used in step 18. Each animal needs its upward sprinkling first and its downward sprinklings after. רב פפא's plan has the שעיר's downward sprinklings first, so it fails. רבא is frustrated that the lesson was just taught and still not applied.

keyTerms.meaning: Fools
Fools of fools
We teach
They learn
Upward sprinkling / downward sprinkling

steps.whatToRemember: For every animal, upward comes first and downward comes after. Any plan for mixed blood must keep that order for both the פר and the שעיר. That is why a full new set for the שעיר is needed.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא's harsh words are not the proof. The actual argument is the last line: the goat's downward sprinklings cannot come before its upward one.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Until now they called us fools,
phrases.notes: The scholars of ארץ ישראל called the Babylonian scholars foolish.

phrases.english: and now, fools of fools,
because we teach them and they do not learn.
But look, he is giving the goat's downward sprinklings
before the goat's upward sprinkling,
and the Torah said:
Give upward, and after that downward!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: עַד הַשְׁתָּא קָרוּ לַן טַפְשָׁאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's proposal from step 21 using the order principle from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's plan to give seven downward sprinklings for both animals before the שעיר's upward one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah requires upward before downward for each animal. רב פפא's plan gives the שעיר's downward sprinklings before its upward one, so it breaks the required order.
